MESF 5010.title: Foundation of Solid Mechanics
MESF 5010.description: Continuum concept for deformation of solids; analysis of stress and strain; constitutive equations; solution of problems relevant to materials processing, fracture mechanics and structural analysis; energy methods and numerical solutions.
cilos: Apply solid mechanics knowledge to advanced stress analysis and practical problems.
Explain some solid mechanics related phenomena in engineering and daily life.
Perform quantitative analysis for practical solid mechanics problems.

MESF 5050.title: Fracture Behavior of Polymers
MESF 5050.description: Introduction to both fundamental and practical knowledge on the microstructure, physical and mechanical behaviors, particularly the fracture behavior and toughening mechanisms, of polymers and composites. Discussions and critiques on related research activities in the literature. Case studies to help students prepare for the industry.
cilos: Explain the microstructure-property relationships of polymers and select proper polymeric materials for specific engineering applications.
Characterize polymer fracture and evaluate fracture toughness of polymers using rigorous fracture mechanics methods under various conditions.
Explain the fundamental fractography of polymers and carry out basic failure analysis using microscopes and thermal analysis equipment.

MESF 5210.title: Fluid Dynamics
MESF 5210.description: Basic concepts of fluid flows, derivation of governing equations, viscous flow, potential flow, boundary layer, flow instability, transition to turbulence, turbulent boundary layer.
cilos: Apply fluid mechanics knowledge to certain practical problems.
Explain some fluid mechanics related phenomena in daily life.
Analyze practical fluid mechanics problems.

MESF 5370.title: Composites and Nanocomposites
MESF 5370.description: This course is designed to provide fundamental understanding of fiber-reinforced composites (FRPs) and emerging nanocomposites technologies. The topics include constituent materials, microstructure-property relationships, fabrication and processing techniques, fundamental mechanics of stress transfer, lamination theory and failure mechanisms and fracture of FRPs in the first part. The topics in the second part include synthesis of nanoscale reinforcements, fabrication and processing techniques of nanocomposites; dispersion and functionalization of nanoreinforcements; interfacial adhesion; mechanical and functional properties of nanocomposites, and their design and applications.
cilos: Distinguish different fabrication and processing methods for FRPs and nanocomposites.

Explain the mechanical and functional properties of these composites based on the microstructures/properties of the fillers and the matrix material, as well as the way how these constituents are combined to produce composites.
Identify potential applications of FRPs and nanocomposites utilizing these properties.
Identify the mechanics of stress transfer through the filler/matrix interface and interphase, lamination theory and failure mechanisms behind the fracture of FRPs and nanocomposites.

MESF 5380.title: Advanced Numerical Methods in Engineering
MESF 5380.description: This is an advanced level course in numerical methods, targeted at graduate students of engineering majors. It will teach fundamental math and algorithms of numerical methods such as analysis of errors, roots of equations, linear and algebraic equation systems, optimizations, curve-fitting and approximation, numerical differentiation and integration, ordinary differential equations, and partial differential equations. In addition, the students will have tutorials in scientific programming tools such as MATLAB and Excel VBA and learn how to use them to implement their own numerical methods.
cilos: Recognize the commanding knowledge in fundamental mathematics and algorithms underneath today's popular numerical methods.
Apply basic MATLAB computer programming to implement some representative numerical methods.
Describe the history and evolution of the technologies and innovations in mechanical engineering.
Describe and formulate a mechanical engineering problem in a format suitable for solution by numerical methods.

MESF 5430.title: Thermodynamics and Kinetics of Materials
MESF 5430.description: An advanced treatment of the thermodynamics, kinetics and transport properties in solids, solutions, surfaces, and heterogeneous reactions.
cilos: Examine the materials and materials processes from the perspective of both thermodynamics and kinetics.
Identify the laws of thermodynamics and solution theory of materials.
Explain the diffusion and phase transformation in terms of its kinetics.
Explain the effect of thermodynamics and kinetics on the microstructure of materials.

MESF 5450.title: Intermediate Heat and Mass Transfer
MESF 5450.description: The scope of this course is intended to establish the conservation laws of heat and mass transfer, with the aims to provide the required knowledge for industrial applications. The topics in a sequential sense covers: Concepts of continuum in multiscale thermal and mass flow systems; Definitions of thermodynamics properties; Conservation equations of fluid flow and heat and mass transfer; Dimensional analyses; Heat conduction and mass diffusion; Convective heat and mass transfer; Computational heat and mass transfer; Special topics and industrial applications.
cilos: Describe in-depth the concepts of continuum through statistical physics.
Apply the conservation laws to fluid flows and transports of heat and mass.
Demonstrate the dimensionless parameters that play the key roles in heat and mass transfer.
Illustrate the basic physics of transport phenomena through the analytical solutions of simple heat and mass transfer problems.
Apply the numerical technique for solving the practical engineering problems where the analytical solutions are not available.

MESF 5520.title: Fundamental Theories and Algorithms of CAD/CAM/CAE
MESF 5520.description: Representations of curves and surfaces, geometric modeling, mesh generation algorithms, optimization algorithms, NC machining part programming, NC machining tool path generation algorithms, digital manufacturing.
cilos: Explain the fundamental mathematical theories and algorithms underlying modern CAD/CAM/CAE systems/technologies.
Use a computer language (e.g. MATLAB) to implement some classical algorithms in curves, surfaces, optimization, and numerical controlled machining tool path generation.

MESF 5550.title: Robotics
MESF 5550.description: Introduce the basic concepts related to industrial robots.  Course will cover the following contents: rigid body motion, forward and inverse kinematics, manipulator jacobians, force relation, dynamics and position control robot manipulators, force control and trajectory generation, collision avoidance and motion planning, robot programming languages.
cilos: Describe the basics of robotic systems.
Define the needs, acquire necessary information and select appropriate robots for various industrial applications.
Apply the knowledge learned for the design and development of simple robots.
Explain the principles of robot kinematics, dynamics, motion planning, trajectory generation and control.

MESF 5560.title: Precision Manufacturing Technologies
MESF 5560.description: Principles of precision engineering; mathematical definitions and theoretical studies of 2D precision assemblies; micro- and nano- positioning for precision machining; nanometrology, data processing for precision measurement; dynamic control for precision machining of engineering materials, applications and industrial practices.
cilos: Use basic knowledge in mechanisms and mathematical tool to model to design products with quality.
Conduct tolerance allocation and analysis for precision machine design and assessment.
Conduct sensibility analysis for precision design optimization.
Evaluate the needs and benefits of precision manufacturing technologies.
Recognize the technical and social problems in the manufacturing industries in the Pearl River Delta and the need for industrial transformation.

MESF 5570.title: Precision Machining
MESF 5570.description: Basic concepts of precision machining; tribosystems of abrasive machining processes; kinematic models; contact mechanics; force, friction, and energy; thermal design; molecular dynamics; tribochemistry of abrasive machining; abrasive tools and conditioning; methods and systems of fixed and free abrasive technology for micro- and nano- precision machining and fabrication applications; advanced applications of abrasive technology such as free form machining and micro fabrication.
cilos: Apply the process models of precision machining, such as kinematics, mechanics, force, friction, energy, thermal design, and tribochemistry, for precision machining process design.
Evaluate the key factors affecting surface quality in precision machining.
Analyze the types of machining tools and their characteristics for machining process design.
Evaluate the relationships between precision, energy efficiency, thermal damage, and cost, with the machining parameters, for machine tool design and development.

MESF 5580.title: Topology Optimization and Additive Manufacturing
MESF 5580.description: This course focuses on analysis and optimal design techniques and fabrication methods of structures and devices. The underlying principles of calculus of variations, constrained minimization, and design parameterization and solution methods of topology optimization will be fully studied. Key applications include mechanical metamaterials, compliant structures/mechanisms and multi-material soft robots. The course will bring out methodologies for designing optimal materials/structures/machines and fabrication techniques of 3D printing.
cilos: Recognize the commanding knowledge in fundamental mathematics and algorithms underneath today’s topology optimization methods.
Apply basic MATLAB computer programming to implement some representative numerical methods.
Describe the history and evolution of the technologies and innovations in mechanical engineering.
Describe and formulate a mechanical engineering problem in a format suitable for solution by design optimization methods.

MESF 5930.title: Finite Element Methods
MESF 5930.description: Finite element formulation; variational principles for structural and continuum mechanics; numerical interpolation and integration; plane stress and plane strain analysis; plate bending and three dimensional solids; solution of large systems of algebraic equations.
cilos: Derive finite element formulations for structural mechanical problems and heat conduction.
Implement finite element methods for simple 1-D problems such as truss analysis and 1-D heat conduction either by hand calculation or by programming.
Numerically evaluate stresses, strains and deformation of a structural component due to axial load, torsion, and bending, acting individually or in combination.
Numerically calculate temperature profile and heat flux in 1-D and 2-D heat conduction problems.
Numerically evaluate stresses, strains and deformation of a structure under either plane-stress or plane-strain conditions.
Derive finite element formulations for time-dependent and/or non-linear problems.
Perform structural analysis and heat transfer modeling using commercial software package, and conduct engineering design in a team work environment.

MESF 5940.title: Advanced Materials Analytics
MESF 5940.description: This course focuses on advanced materials analytics, including roles of engineering materials, material processing and their properties in products and manufacturing. Process selection analytics with focuses on product type, product volume, designs, precision and usage will be emphasized.
cilos: Introduce the relationships among the engineering material properties and process variables in a given manufacturing process.
Understand the principles of traditional and recently developed manufacturing processes.
Provide process characteristics, capabilities and limitations on related machinery and equipment.
Analyze and make decisions in manufacturing and product specifications.

MESF 5950.title: Mechanical Properties and Microstructure of Materials
MESF 5950.description: This course is an introductory course under the umbrella of the materials science topics, specialized for mechanical properties and microstructure characterization. It introduces the fundamental laws and physics of structural and functional materials including atomic structures and bonding, crystal structures and symmetry, mechanical properties and mechanical tests, microstructure characterization, defects in solids, strengthen mechanisms and diffusion. Specifically, we will highlight the metallic materials and their mechanical properties, deformation mechanisms and enhancement mechanisms.
cilos: Recognize and analyze the various types of microstructure of materials such as dislocations, grain boundaries and twins.
Describe how the mechanical tests are conducted and process the data to obtain the mechanical properties of materials.
Explain the underlying mechanism for the specific physical/mechanical property of the material.
Explain the relationship between the processing parameters and the associated mechanical properties and phenomena such as modulus, ductility and strengthening of metallic materials.

MESF 5970.title: Smart Materials, Sensors and Transducers
MESF 5970.description: Materials have been shaping human history since the dawn of civilization, as the naming of eras after materials - the Stone Age, the Bronze Age, the Iron Age - reminds us. Smart materials are a novel class of materials characterized by new and unique properties that can be altered in response to environmental stimuli. They can be used in a wide range of applications since they can exceed the current abilities of traditional materials, especially in environments where conditions are constantly changing. This course is designed to provide an integrated and complete knowledge of smart materials and meta-structures. The course will also introduce the state-of-the-art advances in applications of smart materials in sensors, actuators, energy harvesters, acoustic transducers, and microelectronic and mechanical systems. The course will lay a strong foundation for students' future research and career in electrical engineering, mechanical engineering, and material science.
cilos: Obtain the basic principles of micro manufacturing.
Identify basic materials properties and characterization skills.
Identify basic design and operation principles of sensors, actuators and energy harvesters.

MESF 5980.title: Sustainable Engineering and Energy
MESF 5980.description: This course aims to equip students to address sustainability challenges through engineering. It introduces essential design concepts, tools, and technologies for lean and green manufacturing, sustainable supply chains, and renewable energy. Students will learn to evaluate, design, and maintain environmentally responsible products, processes, services, and policies - preparing them to integrate sustainability into real-world engineering solutions.
cilos: Discuss and argue the impacts of industrial pollution on ecosystem and human health.
Identify local and international industrial pollution regulations and policies.
Interpret life cycle analysis of a product.
Apply the principles and practices of design for environment in consumer products to reduce their total environmental impact.

MESF 6910.title: Special Topics in Mechanical Engineering
MESF 6910.description: Selected topics in mechanical engineering of current interest to the Department in emerging areas and not covered by existing courses.
cilos: Identify the fundamental knowledge of the selected topics of current interest which may not be covered by existing courses.
Design and evaluate the selected topics in different areas.
Apply advanced theories and methods related to the course topic.
Formulate and solve problems in the various areas of the course topic.

MESF 6950.title: Independent Project
MESF 6950.description: An independent research project on Mechanical Engineering carried out under the supervision of a faculty member. May be graded PP.
cilos: Pursue a topic of interest in mechanical engineering area that does not necessarily fit into a traditional academic curriculum.
Analyze specialized materials and gain research/development experience.
Use a holistic view to critically, independently and creatively identify, formulate and deal with complex issues.
Develop a consciousness of the ethical aspects of research and development work.
